tool.name: mumemto extract
tool.command:
ln -s '$m' input.mums && ln -s '$reference' reference.fa &&
## extract_mums only reads the first line of the lengths file and only to pick up the ## FASTA path, so synthesise it rather than rewriting the run's own lengths file. echo 'reference.fa' > input.lengths &&
mumemto extract -m input.mums -l input.lengths -o 'output.fa' ## inverted on purpose: -t is what suppresses the terminator $add_terminator

param.name: reference
param.label: Reference FASTA
param.help: The first FASTA file from the mumemto run. MUM coordinates are taken from this sequence, so it must be the same file that came first in the original run.

param.name: add_terminator
param.label: Append a # terminator to each sequence
param.help: mumemto appends '#' after every MUM sequence by default, which is not valid FASTA. Leave this off unless a downstream tool expects the terminator.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Extracts the actual DNA sequence of every MUM from the original FASTA.
Each MUM's coordinates are read from the **first** sequence of the mumemto run, so the FASTA supplied here has to be the file that came first in that run. Only that one file is needed — the sequences of the other genomes are identical by definition, since a MUM matches everywhere.
If the FASTA holds several records they are concatenated in file order before the coordinates are applied, matching how mumemto indexed them.
**Input**
- A `.mums` file from mumemto - The first FASTA file from that run, plain or gzipped
**Output**
A FASTA file with one record per MUM, named `mum_0`, `mum_1`, and so on in the order they appear in the MUMs file.
By default mumemto appends a `#` terminator to every sequence, which is not valid FASTA; this wrapper suppresses it unless you ask for it back.
